parts.gloss: to the one who does not love

words.gloss: to the one who does not love

literal: To the one who does not love, intense pain you speak; the ocean you do not dry up; may you live, O heart!
translation: May you prosper, my heart! You reveal your deep torment to him who does not love you; why do you not rather try to dry up the roaring ocean that torments me?
modern: என் நெஞ்சே! நீ வாழ்க! உன்னிடம் அன்பு காட்டாதவரிடம் உன்னுடைய மிகுந்த துன்பத்தைச் சொல்கிறாய்; அதற்குப் பதிலாக, உன்னைத் துன்புறுத்தும் இந்தக் கடலை வற்றச் செய்யாமல் இருக்கிறாயே!
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her own heart in deep distress. She notes that her heart keeps yearning for and trying to communicate its intense suffering to her beloved, who remains indifferent and does not return her love. She sarcastically blesses her heart and suggests that trying to dry up the vast, roaring ocean—which worsens her grief with its relentless sound—would be just as futile, yet perhaps a better task than pleading with an unfeeling lover. The word 'செறாஅஅய்' is used here in the sense of drying up or scooping out the ocean, highlighting the impossibility and desperation of her situation.
